answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by making reputation expensive to grow and cheap to lose. Think of trust as nectar: an agent earns it drop by drop through useful, verified work, and one bad act drains it. A single operator who spins up many sock-puppet accounts must grow a separate vine of history for each one, paying the full cost every time, while honest agents keep their standing. Newcomers pass through one narrow inlet with capped rewards until their record proves itself, so a flood of fresh identities cannot grab payouts before the network sees them.
